verdict_reason: Repaired and verified end-to-end. Byte ownership was produced by splitting shared character-offset spans EVENLY and was labelled exact; a byte-level BPE reports the same span for every piece of one character, so no arithmetic on offsets can recover ownership. Real GPT-2 on the emoji string has true piece ownership [3,1,1] (verified against the released byte-level alphabet, and the pieces reconstruct the source UTF-8 exactly: 5 of 5 bytes), where the even split gave [2,2]. Driving the real strided_perplexity: scored bytes are now 2 (was 3) and bits_per_byte 12.215392 against the reference 12.215388353192 (rel 3.4e-7, float32 forward noise) where it had been 8.143592 (-33.3%); the sentence case gives 49 scored bytes (was 50) and 1.4731944 against 1.473194823257. Attribution mode is reported as token_pieces on a real gpt2 run.
comparable_reason: bits_per_byte and bits_per_char are bit-identical on any ASCII-only corpus (measured 0.1893004524905717 for both on a gpt2 run), so they are perfectly collinear columns unless the corpus carries multi-byte characters.
github_reason: Piece ownership derived from the released GPT-2 byte-level alphabet and verified to reconstruct the source UTF-8 exactly; tests/tasks/test_perplexity_byte_ownership.py (7 assertions) plus 3 existing parity assertions.
confounds_reason: When ownership cannot be established the task now WITHHOLDS bits_per_byte rather than fabricating a denominator -- verified: with the piece route disabled, an ASCII corpus keeps the exact offsets partition (41 bytes) while an emoji corpus falls back to full_corpus_upper_bound instead of an invented number.
